facts.fact: The Federal Government, through the National Population Commission with UNICEF support, introduced the Electronic Birth Registration system to digitise birth registration, and the partnership behind it produced the Vital Registration (VitalReg) application; the document describes births only and gives no date, so its publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Birth Registration (eBR) system; VitalReg application

facts.fact: The National Population Commission's focal person in Gwarzo, Kano State, says the digital platform issues the certificate immediately after a successful registration, at registration points designated in each ward, and the application is described as interoperable with the NIN system and other national databases; where the record is held is not stated. Undated, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Birth Registration (eBR) system; VitalReg application

facts.fact: The system was introduced by the Federal Government through the National Population Commission with UNICEF support, in a partnership of the Commission, NIMC, ALGON, Banksforte Technologies Limited and UNICEF that produced the VitalReg application; undated, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Birth Registration (eBR) system; VitalReg application

facts.fact: A 2026 programme to accelerate birth registration in Kano State, pairing digital registration with community mobilisation, is funded by the Government of the Netherlands, and the system itself was introduced with UNICEF support; the document names no domestic budget line. The publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Birth Registration (eBR) system; VitalReg application

systems.system: Electronic Birth Registration (eBR) system; VitalReg application

systems.tiers: decentralised to ward and community level; designated registration points in each ward of Gwarzo local government area, Kano State; registration centres formerly mostly at local government areas

systems.system: Accelerating Birth Registration and Leave No Child Behind in Nigeria 2026
systems.owner: National Population Commission and UNICEF, funded by the Government of the Netherlands
systems.tiers: Kano State; in Gwarzo local government area more than 3,600 of 10,000 targeted children aged one and under registered, at gatherings such as a ward head's residence
